recipe_version.title: Tuscan Panzanella with White Beans and Basil
recipe_version.description: A summer bread salad as a full dinner: oven-toasted chunks of crusty bread soaking up the juices of salted ripe tomatoes, cucumber, and red onion in a garlicky red wine vinaigrette, with creamy white beans, capers, and lots of basil.

ingredients.name: crusty bread
ingredients.display_name: day-old ciabatta or country loaf with no milk or butter

ingredients.name: kosher salt
ingredients.note: 1 tsp tomatoes, 1/4 tsp bread, 1/2 tsp dressing

steps.title: Preheat and prep
steps.body: Turn the oven on to 400 F to preheat. Tear the bread into 1-inch pieces. Cut the tomatoes into chunks, toss with 1 tsp salt, and put them in a colander set over a bowl to catch the juices. Slice the cucumber and red onion. Drain the beans.

steps.title: Toast the bread
steps.body: Toss the bread with 3 tbsp olive oil and 1/4 tsp salt on the sheet pan and bake in the preheated 400 F oven until golden and crisp outside, 10 to 12 minutes, shaking the pan once. The tomatoes keep draining during the toast (overlap stated: their juices become the dressing).

steps.title: Make the dressing
steps.body: Whisk about 1/4 cup of the collected tomato juice with the vinegar, garlic, 5 tbsp olive oil, 1/2 tsp salt, and the pepper.

steps.title: Toss and rest
steps.body: In a large bowl toss the warm bread, tomatoes, cucumber, onion, beans, capers, and most of the basil with the dressing. Rest 5 minutes so the bread drinks in the juices, then scatter the remaining basil and serve.
